<reason>A established the decisive distinction between mandatory advance assessment and mandatory strengthening. Its alternative addressed B's externality concerns by withholding approval until actual shortfalls were resolved, while allowing already-adequate arrangements to remain unchanged. B offered a plausible proportionality defense but never explained why already-binding safeguards needed strengthening. Instead, it repeatedly portrayed A as permitting approval before mitigation, even after A explicitly ruled that out. A answered both pressure questions directly and carried its comparative advantage through the closing.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B conceded that genuinely comprehensive advance assessment would produce no different approvals. A then showed that attaching already-enforceable plans closes no demonstrated gap: B either accepts unchanged safeguards, abandoning mandatory strengthening, or imposes an additional hurdle without additional protection.</best_rebuttal>
